author: marcfeuermann
body: Done. Once again, the sequences seemed to be in the wrong family. I do not understand why this happens so often with pombe sequences....

author: ValWood
body:
I think it is likely because the clustering will try to cluster with fungi by default. But in many cases there is gene loss in the cerevisiae clade and pombe retains the gene, so it has a direct human counterpart which is not present in other yeast.

In this case pombe Csn4 == Human COPS4 

Really [PTHR10855](http://www.pantherdb.org/panther/lookupId.jsp?id=PTHR10855)
should be split into  separate orthologous groups


19S proteasome regulatory subunit Rpn5
AND
COP9/signalosome complex subunit Csn4

It's  also weird because in DIOPT the panther prediction is correct:
https://www.flyrnai.org/cgi-bin/DRSC_orthologs.pl?input_species=4896&output_species=0&additional_filter=None&search_fields=***&search_datasets=***&gene_list=SPAC22A12.03c
